sources.title: Repository tagged three-thread ABC interview question
Independent timed concurrency stress and cancellation validation

claims.text: The preserved source requires only three threads taking turns to print A, B and C; rounds, Java API and cancellation policy are not specified.
Under the explicit A-first/equal-round contract, the exact candidate Java fence produces strict ABC repetition and terminates across fixed and randomized concurrent runs.
The implementation blocks on Semaphore permits instead of busy waiting and maintains constant synchronization state; the test-oriented returned output itself grows with rounds.
The declared caller-interruption path propagates InterruptedException and interrupts worker threads; richer production failure coordination remains outside the preserved source contract.

validation.command: extract exact candidate Java; javac -Xlint:all -Werror; execute timed exact-order stress and caller-interruption leak check
validation.reported_stdout: PASS fixed=7 exact_cases=507 random=500 exact-order=pass no-deadlock=pass negative=reject caller-interrupt=propagated workers=terminated
checks: exact candidate Java compiles with warnings as errors
500 seeded randomized round counts produce exact ABC repetition
caller interruption propagates and printer workers terminate

boundary_tests.expected: empty output and all three threads terminate
observable output remains exact ABC repetition
propagate InterruptedException and interrupt all workers

findings: The preserved repository source says only “算法：三个线程轮流打印 A、B、C”; it does not specify repetition count, Java API, busy-wait policy, or cancellation/error semantics.
The candidate preserves that sparse boundary and explicitly labels A-first order, equal rounds, Java, zero/negative-round handling, and caller-interruption behavior as answer-side contracts.
The three-Semaphore topology correctly implements a single logical token: A starts with one permit, B/C with zero, and every normal print transfers eligibility only to the unique successor A→B→C→A.
Because a thread must acquire its dedicated permit before appending, scheduler start/run order cannot make B or C observably print ahead of the predecessor on the normal path; no busy spin is used.

The returned StringBuilder result is read only after joins; the candidate correctly distinguishes O(rounds) returned-output space from O(1) synchronization state rather than claiming total O(1) memory.
Reviewer-owned validation extracts the exact candidate Java fence and executes 507 timed exact-output cases, including 500 seeded randomized round counts, with no deadlock and exact ABC repetition.

An independent cancellation probe interrupts the caller during a million-round invocation, confirms InterruptedException propagation, and verifies all named printer worker threads terminate rather than leaking.

The answer appropriately states that production failure propagation/output-action failure would require an additional contract; no fabricated production experience, placeholder implementation, or uncovered source variant was found.
